papers.title: What constrains the neutron-star crust? Present data, future measurements, and EOS doppelg"angers
papers.micro: Forecasts centred on a single reference equation of state show that more precise measurements of radius, tidal deformability, and total moment of inertia mainly constrain crust thickness.
papers.abstract: The neutron-star crust plays a central role in pulsar glitches, thermal evolution, and stellar oscillations, yet its properties remain difficult to constrain. We use Bayesian inference with a unified crust-core equation of state to assess what present nuclear and astrophysical data tell us about the crust and what future stellar measurements can add. Within this model, present crust constraints are dominated by chiral effective field theory, with laboratory data providing additional information and current stellar observations having a smaller effect. The adopted theoretical bands determine how tightly the crust properties are constrained, while the treatment of neutron-rich surface energy affects their inferred values. Forecasts centred on a single reference equation of state show that more precise measurements of radius, tidal deformability, and total moment of inertia mainly constrain crust thickness. They provide little additional information about the crust-core transition, crust mass, or crustal moment of inertia and do not recover the precision lost when the chiral effective field theory constraint is removed. Two models with nearly identical global stellar observables can have crust masses and crustal moments of inertia differing by about a factor of two, yet remain indistinguishable at the assumed precision. Precise global measurements therefore need not uniquely determine the crust. Observations that directly probe the crust are needed to distinguish these models.

papers.title: Numerical experiments on sunspot penumbral flows
papers.micro: We present 3D radiative magnetohydrodynamic simulations of sunspots with a self-consistently generated penumbra.
papers.abstract: We present 3D radiative magnetohydrodynamic simulations of sunspots with a self-consistently generated penumbra. We analyze the impact of resolution, surrounding opposite-polarity fields and subsurface large-scale flows on the structure and stability of the simulated penumbra. Extended penumbral filaments are obtained for a subset of the simulations. These were run at 25 km (15 km) horizontal (vertical) resolution and with initial conditions favoring fields with strong horizontal components in the penumbral region. The surface velocities in these simulations are consistent with observations of Evershed flow. The main driving mechanism remains the same as illustrated previously in Rempel (2012). The most successful simulations produce extended penumbrae using a potential magnetic field top boundary, in contrast to previous simulations of extended penumbra with an artificial enhancement of horizontal magnetic field at the top boundary.

papers.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1): Performance of the redshift measurement and spectroscopic analysis
papers.micro: For high-quality samples selected in the EDF-N, we find a 98.5% agreement between Euclid and DESI spectroscopic redshifts.
papers.abstract: The European Space Agency's Euclid mission has issued its first major data release(Data Release 1, DR1), providing a transformative view of the extragalactic sky through deep photometry and near-infrared slitless spectroscopy. This paper presents the Euclid DR1 spectroscopic data set and details the evolution of the spectroscopic processing function (SPE PF) pipeline, which is responsible for the automated analysis of 1-dimensional spectra acquired by the Near-Infrared Spectro-Photometer (NISP). The SPE PF pipeline workflow comprises spectroscopic classification, redshift determination, and the systematic measurement of spectral features. Emission line fluxes are derived using two independent methodologies: direct integration (DI) and Gaussian fitting (GF). For sources exhibiting broad Hα profiles (velocity dispersion larger than 1500 km s⁻¹), a dedicated `QSO mode' is implemented to robustly deconvolve nuclear and host galaxy components. The data set was validated by cross-matching Euclid results with external spectroscopic catalogues, specifically Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) DR1, and through an extensive visual inspection campaign of approximately 4000 sources within the Euclid Deep Field North (EDF-N). For high-quality samples selected in the EDF-N, we find a 98.5% agreement between Euclid and DESI spectroscopic redshifts. This success rate increases to 98.9% when incorporating pipeline probability and reliability estimators. (abridged)

papers.title: Evidence for a Fast, Long-Period, Hot Population of Accreting Neutron Stars
papers.micro: A non-linear deterministic braking mechanism can instead shift and compress a spin distribution, but the spin data alone do not identify the braking mechanism.
papers.abstract: Context. Accreting neutron stars in low-mass X-ray binaries allow us to probe the accretion histories that produce recycled millisecond pulsars. Aims. We expand the analysis of the spin distribution with an enlarged sample of 39 accreting neutron stars and investigate whether the high-frequency objects preferentially occur in binaries with longer orbital periods and have higher quiescent surface temperatures. Methods. We compare several empirical models for the spin distribution. We use stochastic drift-diffusion estimates and simple braking models to determine whether short-timescale torque fluctuations or secular spin-down can account for the observed population widths. Results. The best statistical description of the spin distribution consists of a broad low-frequency component and a narrow high-frequency concentration centred at  566 Hz with a width of  32 Hz. Fast rotators preferentially occupy longer orbital-period binaries, with possibly higher neutron star temperatures. Short-timescale stochastic accretion torque fluctuations cannot produce the observed spin-frequency dispersion in either the fast or the slow component, even under generous assumptions. We show that a non-linear deterministic braking mechanism can instead shift and compress a spin distribution, but the spin data alone do not identify the braking mechanism. Conclusions. The population widths appear to reflect differences in long-term torque conditions and/or evolutionary histories rather than short-timescale torque noise. If the fast systems are close to spin equilibrium, their narrow distribution requires the combination of physical parameters setting the equilibrium frequency to vary relatively little from source to source.Any model that explains the spin distribution should therefore also explain why the fast systems tend to have longer orbital periods and, possibly, higher temperatures.

papers.title: General δ N formalism in Single Field Inflation and Graph Theory
papers.micro: For transitions without a potential step, we derive an explicit all-order expression for the vertex amplitudes and establish their positivity and dependence on the sharpness of the transition.
papers.abstract: We study higher order correlation functions in single field inflation using the δN formalism and methods from graph theory. By representing connected tree level contributions as graphs, we systematically classify their independent topologies, momentum shapes and amplitudes. We show that the amplitudes of arbitrary trees factorize into products of primary amplitudes, providing a general framework for relations among higher order correlators, including the Suyama-Yamaguchi equality. As the number of external legs increases, the number of distinct tree topologies grows exponentially, whereas the number of algebraically distinct amplitude products grows considerably more slowly. As an application, we consider ultra-slow-roll inflation followed by a transition to a slow-roll attractor. For transitions without a potential step, we derive an explicit all-order expression for the vertex amplitudes and establish their positivity and dependence on the sharpness of the transition. When a potential step is included, we prove that all nonlinear vertex amplitudes remain positive for upward steps, whereas downward steps allow cancellations at specific parameter values. These cancellations can eliminate entire families of tree contributions, including configurations in which the leading local bispectrum and trispectrum vanish simultaneously while higher order correlations remain nonzero.

papers.title: Asteroseismology of blue straggler stars in ω Centauri. Stellar collisions as a possible formation scenario
papers.micro: We identify three evolutionary behaviours: no, delayed, and immediate rejuvenation.
papers.abstract: Context. Blue stragglers are intriguing stars that appear more massive and younger than expected from single-star evolution, yet their evolutionary histories remain elusive because of the multiple possible formation channels. A promising and poorly explored avenue for addressing this problem is asteroseismology, which provides the most stringent constraints on internal structure and evolution. Aims. We investigate five SX Phoenicis stars from the core of the globular cluster ωCentauri that pulsate in two radial modes and occupy the blue-straggler region of the colour-magnitude diagram. Seismic models are constructed assuming a collisional origin and compared with our previous seismic studies based on single-star evolution. For comparison, we also explore a binary-evolution scenario involving mass transfer for one of the stars. Methods. The evolution of the parent stars is computed with MESA. The collision is then modelled with the MMAMS code, which reconstructs the merger remnant using an entropic variable. The subsequent evolution is followed with MESA up to the current age of the cluster. Finally, we construct seismic models reproducing the observed frequencies of the two radial modes. Results. We present the first seismic modelling of SX Phe stars (blue stragglers) based on the collision-formation scenario. Convective-core overshooting is essential for rejuvenation and for obtaining seismic models in the main-sequence phase of evolution, but it is not always sufficient. Whether a merger remnant undergoes rejuvenation depends in a complex way on the masses of the parent stars, metallicity, and collision time. We identify three evolutionary behaviours: no, delayed, and immediate rejuvenation. The collisional seismic models imply younger ages and higher masses than the seismic models based on single-star evolution.

papers.title: WISE-VAULT: Decade-long Mid-Infrared Variability of WISE AGN
papers.micro: We identify 632,939 variable AGNs, including 54,897 sources that exhibit large-amplitude variability (ΔW1 > 0.5 mag) and 624 with extreme intrinsic variability (Avar > 0.5 mag).
papers.abstract: Mid-infrared (MIR) variability provides a powerful probe of accretion processes and dust reprocessing in active galactic nuclei (AGNs), as it is less affected by extinction than optical flux. Using multi-epoch photometry from WISE and NEOWISE spanning over a decade, we investigate the MIR variability of ∼4.5 million color-selected AGNs. Variability is quantified using maximum–minimum amplitudes (ΔW1), excess variance, reduced χ², and structure function (SF) analysis over timescales of 0.5–10 years. We identify 632,939 variable AGNs, including 54,897 sources that exhibit large-amplitude variability (ΔW1 > 0.5 mag) and 624 with extreme intrinsic variability (Avar > 0.5 mag). A subset of these sources shows flare-like behavior, identifying them as candidate changing-look AGNs or tidal disruption events that warrant further spectroscopic and multi-wavelength follow-up. The SF analysis shows radio-detected AGNs exhibit the highest variability amplitudes, followed by X-ray detected and the overall AGN sample. The variability amplitude is strongly anti-correlated with the Eddington ratio, indicating enhanced variability in lower accretion rate systems. A weak positive dependence on radio-loudness further suggests a contribution from non-thermal emission in radio sources. These results demonstrate that MIR variability provides a robust diagnostic of accretion physics and an efficient means of identifying extreme and rapidly evolving AGN phenomena. The full catalog of variable AGNs is made publicly available.

papers.title: Symbolic Regression Fitting for Roche Lobe Radius
papers.micro: We present a compact approximation to the dimensionless, volume-equivalent Roche lobe radius RL/a, obtained by applying symbolic regression to radii calculated from the full Roche potential.
papers.abstract: We present a compact approximation to the dimensionless, volume-equivalent Roche lobe radius RL/a, obtained by applying symbolic regression to radii calculated from the full Roche potential. Over 10⁻⁵≤ q≤10⁵, the expression reduces the root mean square error from 1.97×10⁻³ for Eggleton's formula to 5.95×10⁻⁴, while its maximum relative error is 1.39%, compared with Eggleton's 0.83%. Calculations at additional mass ratios give a mean relative error of 0.331%. The formula is monotonic, recovers the q^(1/3) scaling at small mass ratio, and approaches a large-mass-ratio limit within 0.036% of the limiting Roche model. In a NumPy float64 benchmark of 10⁷ direct formula evaluations, the SR expression takes 0.217 s compared with 0.450 s for Eggleton, a speed-up of 2.08. These results quantify the accuracy and evaluation cost of a compact algebraic alternative for binary-system calculations.

papers.title: Unsupervised Machine Learning Classification of FRB 20121102A across Distinct Active Episodes: Implications for FRB Emission Physics and Source Environments
papers.micro: These results suggest that this cluster may represent a distinct burst population potentially associated with different emission physics.
papers.abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are millisecond-duration radio transients of extragalactic origin. Identifying distinct burst populations and investigating their variations across active episodes provide important insights into the physical origins of repeating FRBs. In this paper, we apply an unsupervised machine learning approach to bursts from three active episodes of FRB 20121102A observed by the Five-hundred-metre Aperture Spherical Telescope (FAST). Our analysis reveals four distinct clusters primarily distinguished by their spectral properties. Notably, Cluster 1 exhibits bimodal-like distributions in central frequency and bandwidth and contains nearly all high-energy bursts, with a mean energy about an order of magnitude higher than those of the other clusters. It also occupies a distinct region in the width–fluence parameter space. These results suggest that this cluster may represent a distinct burst population potentially associated with different emission physics. Furthermore, the fractions of different burst clusters vary across active episodes. Cluster 1 accounts for about 27% of the bursts in 2019, compared with about 8% in 2022 and 2023. Cluster 2, with higher central frequencies and narrower bandwidths, has the largest fraction in 2019 and 2022, whereas Cluster 3, with broader bandwidths and intermediate central frequencies, has the largest fraction in 2023. These variations may indicate changes in the physical conditions of the emission regions or the local propagation environment across active episodes.

papers.title: Separability defects in artificial satellite theory: intermediaries, zonal harmonics and secular separatrices
papers.micro: For every axisymmetric field the radial defect is linear, with a torque form…
papers.abstract: A five-input Poisson-bracket operator, which reproduces the Levi-Civita separability expressions and is cubic in the Hamiltonian, is used as a diagnostic of artificial satellite theory, in a modified polar-nodal chart regular at prograde equatorial orbits. For the general intermediary proposed by the author in 2020, covering those of Sterne, Garfinkel, Brouwer, Aksnes, Cid and Lahulla and Deprit, the linearised defects vanish if and only if the integrability ansatz holds, the condition for additive first-order Hamilton-Jacobi separation in polar-nodal variables. Second-order defects follow in closed form, and the coupling with the nodal pair comes from the dependence on the physical latitude, shared by the zonal term, Aksnes's intermediary and the originals of Sterne and Garfinkel. For every axisymmetric field the radial defect is linear, with a torque form, and the first-order zonal defect is the operator response to the first-order Lie generator, which also gives the second-order mean radial defect per revolution. In its gauge the long-period second-order average is common to intermediaries without latitude terms. Oblate structures with a displaced centre separate the zonal field exactly if and only if its coefficients satisfy the recurrence of Vinti's translated spheroidal potential, and along orbits propagated over 300 periods in the field truncated at J₄ they conserve the approximate third integral better than the centred structure, by median factors of 23 to 77. On secular separatrices the integrated defect is the derivative of the Melnikov function, tested in the eccentric Kozai-Lidov problem, and transverse zero sets of the operator define event surfaces.

papers.title: Model Choice or Model Bias? How stellar spectral libraries and activity modelling choices influence Ariel spectra- I. Forward model
papers.micro: Library-dependent differences in the facular treatment introduce systematic biases exceeding the Ariel Tier 3 sensitivity threshold of approximately 20 ppm across most of the wavelength range…
papers.abstract: The Ariel mission will conduct a population-level survey of approximately 1000 exoplanet atmospheres across its nominal lifetime, requiring unprecedented consistency in the treatment of stellar contamination of transmission spectra. We present a systematic comparison of stellar spectral libraries and modelling approaches for computing facular and spot contamination spectra across the full Ariel wavelength range (0.5-7.8 microns) for six stellar spectral types spanning F3 to M2. Using a surface resolved forward model with approximately 200 randomly generated active region configurations per spectral type, we compute contamination spectra at Ariel Tier 3 resolution and compare three 1D spectral libraries against 3D MHD stellar atmosphere spectra as a physical ground truth. We find that library-dependent differences in the facular treatment introduce systematic biases exceeding the Ariel Tier 3 sensitivity threshold of approximately 20 ppm across most of the wavelength range, for most spectral types and activity levels considered. These biases align with the absorption bands of water, carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide, and methane, rendering them indistinguishable from genuine atmospheric signals at Ariel's precision. Our results demonstrate hat the choice of stellar spectral library, in particular the faculae treatment is a critical and currently underappreciated source of systematic error for Ariel atmospheric characterisation. The impact on atmospheric retrievals is quantified in a companion paper.

papers.title: Constraining Accretion Regimes of Little Red Dots from Their Variability
papers.micro: Comparing with JWST monitoring constraints, we find that the non-detection of LRD variability requires mdot ≳ 30 for MBH∼10⁷ M☉ on a 0.5 yr rest-frame baseline…
papers.abstract: The “little red dots” (LRDs) are photometrically and spectroscopically non-variable on rest-frame baselines of months, with a 5.9σ deficit relative to ordinary active galactic nuclei (AGNs). If we consider LRDs to be accreting black holes, this non-varying could be a clue about the nature of the accretion. Here, we present a general semi-analytic model of variability from super-Eddington (slim) accretion disks. We consider three mechanisms that play crucial roles in the observed variability, viz., advective attenuation, photospheric averaging, and photon diffusion filter. With this, above mdot ∼ a few, the fractional rms collapses steeply with mdot. Comparing with JWST monitoring constraints, we find that the non-detection of LRD variability requires mdot ≳ 30 for MBH∼10⁷ M☉ on a 0.5 yr rest-frame baseline; a Monte Carlo forward model of the TWINKLE non-detections of 18 LRDs sharpens this to mdot≳60 at 95% confidence. On current baselines, these non-detections remain formally degenerate with a frozen sub-Eddington disk (mdot≲0.1). Longer monitoring will separate the two regimes as the frozen-disk variability grows with baseline, while the super-Eddington collapse does not. The same framework predicts strongly suppressed X-ray variability, testable with future X-ray observatories.

papers.title: PyVesta: A new Versatile Echelle Spectra exTraction and Analysis pipeline
papers.micro: We present PyVesta, an automatic data reduction software for fiber fed echelle spectrographs.
papers.abstract: We present PyVesta, an automatic data reduction software for fiber fed echelle spectrographs. PyVesta is designed to be used with different instruments, both high resolution spectrographs such as HARPS or FEROS as well as inexpensive off-the-shelf spectrographs like the Shelyak eShel II. Special additions were implemented to improve the stability and resolution of inexpensive instruments especially. PyVesta provides tools for all extraction steps from raw CCD images to continuum normalized spectra, e.g., CCD image corrections, spectra extraction, wavelength calibration, and continuum normalization. Our software is based on the software package CERES and was ported to Python 3, revised, and supplemented.

papers.title: 2D and 3D unified RHD atmospheres and wind models of early B-supergiants including approximate NLTE effects
papers.micro: Our calculations suggest that in the lower surface-gravity B supergiants, in addition to modifying the photospheric density scale heights, turbulent pressure also influences global properties of the wind.
papers.abstract: B supergiants are evolved massive stars with low surface gravities and lower effective temperatures, with substantial radiation-driven winds. Generally, they have been studied assuming 1D spherical symmetry. We present the first multi-D unified atmosphere and wind models for B supergiants, especially investigating the effects of approximate NLTE ionization and subsurface turbulence on the atmosphere and wind dynamics. We computed multi-D box-in-a-star RHD unified atmosphere and wind simulations of 2D/3D early B supergiant models using a hybrid opacity approach. We calculated line opacities from approximate NLTE populations, including line scattering. We calculated the flux-, energy-, and Planck-mean line opacities separately from our large line database using Sobolev escape probabilities, assuming two-level atoms. The models develop a highly turbulent atmosphere with time-averaged turbulent velocities of   40 - 55 km/s at the photosphere in the 2D simulations, and   25 km/s in 3D. In the cooler B1, B1.5 models, the wind acceleration is more gradual than in the hotter B0 model, leading to a significantly higher maximum wind speed in the B0 model. Further, the approximate NLTE formalism strongly alters the ionization stratification in the wind compared to LTE, modifying the line force. Mass-loss rates obtained in the models are of order 10^-6 - 3 x 10^-6 solar masses per year. Including turbulent pressure in hydrodynamically consistent NLTE CMF steady-state 1D simulations with comparable parameters can produce higher mass-loss rates and lower terminal wind velocities than in corresponding models without turbulent velocity, in overall qualitative agreement with our multi-D simulations. Our calculations suggest that in the lower surface-gravity B supergiants, in addition to modifying the photospheric density scale heights, turbulent pressure also influences global properties of the wind.

papers.title: Discovery of a Short-Duration Fast X-ray Transient Associated with a Short Gamma-Ray Burst
papers.micro: We report EP260411a, an ∼8-s EFXT discovered in archival Einstein Probe Wide-field X-ray Telescope (EP-WXT) observations through a time-targeted search for X-ray counterparts of short GRBs.
papers.abstract: Extragalactic fast X-ray transients (EFXTs) are an emerging population of high-energy transients with diverse physical origins. Only a few observed EFXTs are associated with compact object mergers, and the known events generally display X-ray emission lasting much longer than their associated short gamma-ray bursts (GRBs). Here we report EP260411a, an ∼8-s EFXT discovered in archival Einstein Probe Wide-field X-ray Telescope (EP-WXT) observations through a time-targeted search for X-ray counterparts of short GRBs. This fast X-ray transient is temporally coincident with short GRB 260411A, with both the pulse width and peak time showing clear anticorrelations with the characteristic photon energy across the gamma-ray and soft X-ray bands. Joint EP-WXT and Fermi-GBM spectral fitting further shows that the broadband emission can be described by a cutoff power-law model with an additional low-energy spectral break, suggesting a common origin for the single-pulse X-ray and gamma-ray emission. The resulting properties place the event within the Type I GRB region in the Ep,z-Eiso plane, supporting its classification as a compact object merger event. Unlike previously known merger-driven Type I EFXTs with long-lasting X-ray emission, EP260411a reveals that the Type I EFXT population can also extend to the short timescale of a few seconds. Its combination of short duration and hard spectrum occupies a sparsely explored region of the EFXT parameter space, providing a new observational link between short-duration EFXTs and compact object mergers.

papers.title: Cubic Galileon Gravity on Nonlinear Scales with Hi-COLA for LSST Year 1
papers.micro: We present an emulator for the 3D nonlinear matter power spectrum in Cubic Galileon gravity…
papers.abstract: Vera C. Rubin Observatory's Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) is in a prime position to test Modified Gravity (MG) with Weak Lensing (WL) and Large Scale Structure (LSS). However, many nonlinear MG emulators in the literature enforce a ΛCDM background by design, missing where data suggest the most interesting deviations lie. We present an emulator for the 3D nonlinear matter power spectrum in Cubic Galileon gravity, a Horndeski theory with a single additional MG parameter, fφ, that modifies the background, growth, and lensing. Trained on Hi-COLA simulations with Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), the emulator achieves ≲ 2% accuracy for k ≤ 1.2 h Mpc⁻¹ at the fiducial cosmology relative to Hi-COLA, and ≲ 5% relative to full N-body EFT-RAMSES simulations. Additionally, conservative scale cuts excluding angular bins affected by baryonic physics enable unbiased parameter estimation in LSST Year 1 weak lensing and galaxy clustering (3×2pt) forecasts, even when validated against simulated data based on higher-resolution N-body simulations. This demonstrates that, within a simplified LSST Y1 setup and the adopted scale cuts, Hi-COLA-based emulation is sufficient to develop inference infrastructure with Stage IV precision for Horndeski gravity models previously unmodeled on nonlinear scales.

papers.title: A helium-rich mass-donor in a 3.5-hr low mass X-ray binary
papers.micro: We apply a Bayesian model-comparison framework, BEANSP, to a sample of 21 thermonuclear bursts from the accretion-powered millisecond pulsar…
papers.abstract: Binary systems in which a neutron star accretes material from a low-mass stellar companion arise from evolutionary processes that depend sensitively on the progenitor properties. It is usually assumed that the accreted material has approximately solar composition, unless the orbital period is ≲80 min, indicating an "ultracompact" system with a hydrogen deficient donor. However, few constraints on the donor composition are available. Here we apply a Bayesian model-comparison framework, BEANSP, to a sample of 21 thermonuclear bursts from the accretion-powered millisecond pulsar, IGR J17511-3057, to constrain the fuel composition as well as the system parameters. Our analysis strongly indicates an extremely hydrogen- and CNO-deficient fuel composition, with X ≈ 0.03 and ZCNO≈ 4 × 10⁻⁴, unexpected for this system with its relatively long 3.5 hr orbital period. We explore the possible circumstances under which such an object can evolve, and discuss the implications for its history also in light of the three transient outbursts that have been observed to date. Such analyses are finding an unexpectedly wide range in donor compositions, that may help to explain the remarkable diversity in the burst properties of the known burst sources

papers.title: Extended Bayesian Estimation for In-flight Calibration of Space-based Instruments
papers.micro: We obtain valid inferences for other structural parameters of the physics model.
papers.abstract: The ongoing calibration of space-based instruments is essential to ensure accurate measurements of physical quantities such as photon flux. The goal is to obtain a unified photon-flux measurement of a single astronomical source using data obtained with multiple instruments. Calibration involves in-flight adjustments to address discrepancies arising from instrument-specific variations. Taking a statistical approach, we extend a previously proposed additive log-Normal hierarchical model with half-variance correction based on a multiplicative physical model for photon counts. The newly proposed Bayesian hierarchical model can leverage domain-specific priors to account for correlated passbands and integrate information across different instruments, sources, and passbands effectively. The model is fitted using Markov chain Monte Carlo and can provide uncertainty quantification for instrument- and source-specific parameter estimation. Moreover, we obtain valid inferences for other structural parameters of the physics model. We use data derived from Chandra and XMM-Newton X-ray observatories to illustrate the proposed inference procedure.

papers.title: JWST/NIRISS-SOSS Spectroscopic Variability and Auroral Modelling of Warm Ultracool Dwarf LSR J1835+3259
papers.micro: No model atmosphere grid provides a reasonable fit to the average NIRISS spectrum.
papers.abstract: Auroral variability in ultracool dwarfs (UCDs) has been proposed as a key source of optical and infrared modulation, yet its physical origin remains poorly understood. We present JWST Near Infrared Imager and Slitless Spectrograph/Single Object Slitless Spectroscopy (NIRISS/SOSS) time-series spectroscopy of the M8.5 UCD LSR J1835+3259. These observations probe the object's wavelength-dependent rotational variability, providing insight into the atmospheric processes underlying its infrared behaviour. Additional GTC/MEGARA optical spectra reveal that its Hα emission has declined markedly since earlier epochs, suggesting a reduced activity state during the JWST observations. We detect no emission from H₃⁺ or absorption by hydronium in the NIRISS spectra. We use principal component analysis to identify two distinct modes of spectral variability: one dominated by FeH modulation near 1 μm and another contributing broadband variability across the H and K bands. We find that no model atmosphere grid provides a reasonable fit to the average NIRISS spectrum. However, a blended model comprising an M-dwarf photosphere and a cooler blackbody component provides an improved fit to the mean spectrum, the broadband spectral energy distribution and the NIRISS broadband variability. By adding perturbations to PICASO model grids, we demonstrate that a combination of atmospheric heating and non-equilibrium chemistry can successfully mimic a blend of unperturbed photosphere and a blackbody, and that the presence of these effects may explain the unusual spectrum and variability of LSR J1835+3259.

papers.title: Properties of near-surface turbulence in hot, massive stars: Statistical signatures from multi-dimensional models of O-type stars
papers.micro: Although not rigorously proven here, we suggest that this steepening is due to the scale-dependent effect of radiative damping.
papers.abstract: Variability of massive stars indicates the presence of complex, multi-D physics near the surface. Recent advancements in multi-D radiation-hydrodynamical modelling of massive star atmospheres show strong turbulence triggered by the iron opacity bump. We analyze statistical properties of sub-surface turbulence in multi-D simulations of O-star atmospheres. Particularly, we study potential dependencies of turbulent properties on global stellar parameters. Using 2D O-star models, we studied several statistical properties of the turbulence that develops in these models. We compute autocorrelation functions of density and velocity to study typical eddy length scales. Moreover, we compute kinetic energy power spectra to analyze the energy distribution and compare this to known results from established turbulence theories. We find anisotropy of the turbulent eddies in velocity space. Moreover, this anisotropy increases with classical Eddington factor. This anisotropy disappears in density space where all models show nearly isotropic structures and no dependence on stellar parameters. The kinetic energy power spectra exhibit an inertial range with a cascade exponent that has an average value of -2.57. This exponent does not show any clear dependence on stellar parameters. Importantly, this energy cascade is significantly steeper than those in known turbulence theories such as Kolmogorov turbulence with exponent -5/3 and Burgers turbulence with exponent -2. This additional steepening can potentially be attributed to radiative damping which increases with increasing wavenumber. Sub-surface turbulence in hot, massive stars is anisotropic and radially dominated in velocity space and its energy cascade is steeper than both Kolmogorov turbulence and Burgers turbulence. Although not rigorously proven here, we suggest that this steepening is due to the scale-dependent effect of radiative damping.

papers.title: Magnetic kink instability of jet-wind outflows. I. Static column configuration
papers.micro: The results indicate that the current-driven kink instability may provide the baryon-loading of AGN jets suggested by the observations.
papers.abstract: We describe the results of computer simulations investigating the stability of an axisymmetric static equilibrium combining a highly magnetised (σ=10³) central column and a mildly (σ=0.1) to weakly (σ=0.001) magnetised outer shell with a helical and mostly force-free magnetic field of constant pitch. The measured linear growth rates of the instability are in agreement with the maximum growth rate for a uniform density column with a force-free magnetic field of constant pitch obtained by Appl et al. (2000), being only a little bit higher. At the non-linear phase, the interface separating the central column and the outer shell develops the characteristic corkscrew shape, with the space inside and between the coils of the corkscrew filled by the shell plasma. In high-resolution runs, a secondary instability is seen as well. It has the form of helical protuberances of low-σ plasma intruding inside the corkscrew coils. These appear to be aligned with the local magnetic field lines. We tentatively identify the secondary instability as the magnetic Rayleigh-Taylor instability. Overall, the results indicate that the current-driven kink instability may provide the baryon-loading of AGN jets suggested by the observations.

papers.title: JCMT–Venus: Daily Monitoring of HDO and SO₂ Absorption in Venus' Mesosphere
papers.micro: Second, long-term variability in H₂O is identified here for the first time and is interpreted as an anticorrelated response to the long-term change in SO₂, likely through H₂SO₄ formation.
papers.abstract: We present three multi-week, disc-integrated James Clerk Maxwell Telescope (JCMT) campaigns monitoring HDO and SO₂ absorption in Venus' upper mesosphere at altitudes of approximately 80–110 km. Obtained in February 2022, July 2023, and August–September 2023, these observations provide dense temporal sampling and complementary observing geometries, enabling the disentanglement of short-term, long-term, and local solar time (LST) variability, which has been challenging in previous studies. We have four main findings. First, SO₂ in the upper mesosphere, being largely absent in February 2022 but present in both 2023 campaigns, may follow the same long-term trend observed at cloud tops. Second, long-term variability in H₂O is identified here for the first time and is interpreted as an anticorrelated response to the long-term change in SO₂, likely through H₂SO₄ formation. Third, H₂O is broadly stable within each campaign, although occasional short-term variability is present in the form of a depletion event. Finally, short-term variability is likely present for SO₂, but it does not dominate the overall behaviour. In the absence of strong long-term differences, the daily SO₂ abundance evolution is consistent with an asymmetric LST profile peaking near midnight, which is well reproduced by an independent model. These results are enabled by a dedicated reduction and retrieval pipeline that mitigates the strong standing-wave baseline structure in the spectra and quantifies systematic uncertainties, providing a methodological framework for future studies facing similar challenges.

papers.title: bihalofit-JAX: A Differentiable Code for the Nonlinear Matter Bispectrum and its Projected Statistics
papers.micro: The pipeline is fully differentiable, and we demonstrate its performance in a simple inference problem, comparing the No-U-Turn Sampler (NUTS) to gradient-free inference with the affine-invariant ensemble sampler (emcee).
papers.abstract: Theoretical predictions for the nonlinear matter bispectrum and related projected statistics have been historically very expensive to evaluate, leading many analyses to rely on emulators to speed up slow numerical codes. We show in this paper that this need not be the case: improved numerical techniques can be leveraged to directly evaluate predictions for the nonlinear matter bispectrum and projected statistics at speeds preferable for inference. We present bihalofit-JAX, an open-source, fully differentiable code for the nonlinear matter bispectrum based on the BiHalofit fitting formula, which includes numerous related projected statistics such as angular bispectra, skew spectra and aperture statistics. It computes 10000 triangles of the matter bispectrum in ∼1–2 ms per cosmology, one to three orders of magnitude faster than other implementations. It agrees numerically with the original BiHalofit code to better than 0.02% on average over the cosmologies the formula was calibrated on, where the formula itself is accurate to ∼20% against simulations. It is also efficiently vectorised such that one can compute e.g. 500 cosmologies in ∼ 2 ms. This speed-up grows even more in the case of the third-order aperture statistics, which we compute in ∼ 6 ms for one cosmology, between 3×10³ and 2.4×10⁴ times faster than other publicly available codes. The pipeline is fully differentiable, and we demonstrate its performance in a simple inference problem, comparing the No-U-Turn Sampler (NUTS) to gradient-free inference with the affine-invariant ensemble sampler (emcee).

papers.title: Extending an X-ray & Mid-Infrared diagnostic for absorption in Active Galactic Nuclei to higher redshifts using NuSTAR and XMM-Newton
papers.micro: We applied the model to the full NSS80 catalogue to determine a statistical measure of the observed Compton thick fraction at fCT=4.9^+2.0_−2.3% to 1σ uncertainty…
papers.abstract: Determining the Compton thick fraction (fCT) within the population of Active Galactic Nuclei (AGN) provides insight into the evolution and growth of Supermassive Black Holes. Measuring fCT requires methods of modelling the AGN column density (NH), typically through spectral fitting which requires high source counts, or estimation methods such as the band ratio. We extend an NH estimation method using the ratio of observed X-ray and MIR luminosity (log(L_2−10keV / L_12μm)), previously applied in the local universe (z<0.1), to a higher redshift. We used a sample of 47 bright AGN from the NuSTAR 80-month catalogue (NSS80) with a median redshift of ⟨ z ⟩ = 0.35 as the high redshift comparison, and we applied X-ray spectral fitting to the NuSTAR sources with physically motivated AGN models to provide NH constraints. The high-z relationship was found to be consistent with the same model as the low-z comparison, but with modestly different parameters which we determined to be due to a higher X-ray luminosity within the NSS80 sample. We applied the model to the full NSS80 catalogue to determine a statistical measure of the observed Compton thick fraction at fCT=4.9^+2.0_−2.3% to 1σ uncertainty, consistent with other recent low-z Swift/BAT measurements.

papers.title: Zeeman-Doppler imaging of V889 Her: Surface spots and magnetic field topology 2017 - 2023
papers.micro: We detect abrupt changes in the spot configuration in June 2018 on the time scale of a week.
papers.abstract: The surface magnetic field of the young solar analogue V889 Her is studied using Zeeman-Doppler imaging (ZDI). This well-studied star has previously been reported to have an exceptionally high differential rotation and show abrupt changes in the surface magnetic field and spot configuration. Our aim is to study the evolution of the magnetic field topology in V889 Her. This will contribute to understanding dynamo action in young solar-type stars. We also want to constrain the surface differential rotation curve of the target star.Methods. We employ the ZDI method on observations collected with the SOFIN spectropolarimeter mounted at the Nordic Optical Telescope. We test differential rotation parameters previously reported in studies of the star. We observe significant changes in the radial field near the rotational pole throughout the whole span of the observations. Specifically, the polarity of the radial field is reversed around 2021. The large-scale magnetic field also contains a persistent strong azimuthal component at high latitudes. We detect abrupt changes in the spot configuration in June 2018 on the time scale of a week. The observations favour a solar type differential rotation. The different rotation parameters influence the brightness map more than the magnetic field topology. We cannot link the observed changes in the magnetic field topology with the evolution of the long-term spot activity. The abrupt changes observed in 2018 confirm previous reports that the surface magnetic field and spot configuration may undergo rapid evolution on short time scales. This complicates the estimation of the surface differential rotation.

papers.title: Density fluctuations in pseudo-streamer and helmet streamer: Generation, propagation and comparison with Metis observations
papers.micro: Unlike in the streamer region, we also find that along the pseudo-streamer axis…
papers.abstract: Recent white-light observations from the Metis coronagraph on board Solar Orbiter have shown the presence of propagating density fluctuations with a period of ∼5 minutes, particularly in the observationally bright regions of helmet streamers and pseudo-streamers. These density fluctuations have been shown to originate from magnetohydrodynamic wave modes – slow and fast modes can directly compress the plasma, whereas Alfvén waves generate density fluctuations via a non-linear coupling with the slow and fast modes. In general, in low plasma β regions, slow modes contribute more towards the generation of density fluctuations, whereas in high β regions, there are significant contributions from both slow and fast waves. In this work, we investigate the propagation of (non-linear) Alfvén waves and the associated density fluctuations using a 2.5D axisymmetric global solar wind model that includes two distinct magnetic field topologies – a helmet streamer and a pseudo-streamer. Key differences in these magnetic configurations give rise to differences in the wave behaviour due to, for example, the presence of a current sheet in the helmet streamer and an X-type null point in the pseudo-streamer, and the structure of the β= 1 layer in both magnetic field configurations. This leads to the possible creation of prominent interference patterns along the helmet streamer axis, which do not appear along the pseudo-streamer axis. Unlike in the streamer region, we also find that along the pseudo-streamer axis, the contribution to the density fluctuations is due to the fast waves only, despite being in a low β plasma.

papers.title: Characterization of the GIGAPYX-4600 CMOS visible image sensor in the context of high precision astrometry
papers.micro: Further improvements are currently being developed for space implementation.
papers.abstract: To evaluate the potential of detectors for next-generation space astrometry missions such as the HWO and Theia, an extensive analysis of the performance of the GIGAPYX-4600 46-megapixel CMOS detector from Pyxalis was conducted at IPAG. The 5456x8320-pixel detector, featuring a 4.4-micron pitch and back-side illumination, constitutes a matrix of 24x36 mm. It has a measured gain of 13.3 electrons per ADU in low-gain mode. The saturation level of the detector in low-gain-mode is estimated to be approximately 52 000 electrons. This sensor demonstrates linearity errors of 0.90%, pixel response non-uniformity of less than 1.3%, and readout and quantization noise of 12 electrons in low-gain mode. Dark current was measured at 35 electrons per second at 35textdegreeC and inter-pixel capacitance remained under 3%. We demonstrated that inter-pixel capacitance effects can be effectively mitigated using spatially varying kernel correction algorithms. Radiation tests confirmed its robustness against protons and heavy ions, and no latch-up was observed. These measurements agree with the manufacturer figures. These characterization results validate the GIGAPYX-4600 as a strong candidate for high-precision astrometry. Further improvements are currently being developed for space implementation.

papers.title: Distinguishing cosmologies with topological analysis of 21-cm hydrogen 2D brightness fields at Cosmic Dawn
papers.micro: However, it can also be a source of observational data for cosmologists seeking to constrain cosmological parameters.
papers.abstract: The 21-cm hydrogen line brightness field is a potentially valuable source of information about astrophysical parameters during the cosmological Dark Ages and the Epoch of Reionization. However, it can also be a source of observational data for cosmologists seeking to constrain cosmological parameters. While much of the effort has been focused on constraining parameters using information across a broad frequency range, most often with the power spectrum of inhomogeneities, we investigate whether a single frequency channel, corresponding to a single redshift slice, can distinguish between cosmological models. We utilize topological data analysis to evaluate the possibility of such constraints. In particular, we use cubical complexes to perform persistent homology analysis of the 21-cm line brightness field. We generate 21-cm brightness fields of different cosmologies with the 21cmFAST package and then select snapshots at several redshifts corresponding to the Epoch of Reionization. Our goal is to find the redshift that is most suitable for highlighting the diversity between scenarios within a certain range of cosmological parameters. To compare persistent pictures built on simulations of the brightness field, we use Wasserstein distance, computed between any two persistent diagrams. We find that observations of the 21-cm field near z=10 have the potential to distinguish between cosmological models with different values of the normalized Hubble parameter h₀, the spectral index of scalar matter perturbations ns, the matter density parameter Ωm, and the matter fluctuation amplitude σ₈, even in the presence of instrumental thermal noise. We perform the PERMANOVA statistical test on the matrices of Wasserstein distances to confirm this hypothesis for all considered cosmological parameters.

papers.title: The effect of vertical mixing on oxygen sequestration by refractory elements in the atmosphere of giant planets
papers.micro: Vertical transport causes magnesium silicates to destabilize already at Teq ∼ 900 K regardless of metallicity, releasing oxygen to H₂O and to minor gas-phase carriers such as SiO and Mg(OH)₂.
papers.abstract: The most widely used route to study the formation history of giant exoplanets is the C/O ratio, usually derived from H₂O, CO, CO₂ and CH₄. However, refractory elements can sequester a significant fraction of O, causing the observed C/O ratio to be overestimated with respect to the intrinsic one. Previous calculations of this bias relied on chemical equilibrium models. Here we quantify the impact of vertical mixing using the 1-D chemical kinetics code VULCAN, expanded with a Mg-Si-Fe network including the condensation and settling of enstatite, forsterite and metallic iron. We compute 168 models spanning equilibrium temperatures Teq ∈ [700, 1500] K, eddy diffusion coefficients Kzz ∈ [10⁶, 10¹⁰] cm² s⁻¹ and metallicities Z ∈ [0.9, 7.2] Z☉, derived self-consistently from planet formation simulations. We find that vertical transport causes magnesium silicates to destabilize already at Teq ∼ 900 K regardless of metallicity, releasing oxygen to H₂O and to minor gas-phase carriers such as SiO and Mg(OH)₂. Therefore, while equilibrium models predict a nearly constant C/O overestimation up to 1100-1300 K, in disequilibrium it drops sharply between 900 and 1200 K. In this transitional range the C/O overestimation is controlled by Kzz and is partially degenerate with metallicity, while outside it is robust against both mixing intensity and the probed atmospheric layer, ranging from 14.5-23% at 700 K to 4.5-7% at 1500 K. Metallic iron condensation prevents Fe from sequestering oxygen, lowering the overestimation by about one third with respect to previous estimates. Finally, CH₄, CO₂ and the CH₄/CO ratio are most sensitive to Kzz in the transitional range, and can provide a constraint on vertical mixing.

papers.title: A New Galactic Close Binary Supersoft Source Candidate
papers.micro: Although there is no current identification of X-ray emission from this source, its SED displays a highly absorbed bright FUV component, given the estimated E(B - V)   0.7 mag.
papers.abstract: The identification of a new galactic Close Binary Supersoft Source (CBSS) candidate, whose main ID is ZTF J043609.49+364057.7, is presented on the basis of the analysis of its optical spectrum, light curve and Spectral Energy Distribution (SED). During a survey designed to find candidates to the aforementioned class independently of X-ray emissions, this object's optical spectrum was found to exhibit the typical emission features expected for a CBSS. The available photometric data show a quasi-sinusoidal modulation, with a period of 5.42 h, compatible with the orbital modulation of the system. Although there is no current identification of X-ray emission from this source, its SED displays a highly absorbed bright FUV component, given the estimated E(B - V)   0.7 mag.

papers.title: Eleven Trans-Neptunian Objects and Eight Candidates Discovered by TESS
papers.micro: We identify eleven new TNOs, each detected blindly in two to five TESS sectors and independently in archival ground-based images, with arcs of 2-20 years.
papers.abstract: We report a blind search for trans-Neptunian objects (TNOs) in Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) full-frame images from 2018 July 25 through 2026 November 6. We search 572 CCD fields near the ecliptic across 95 TESS sectors. After modeling and subtracting Gaia stars with the TESS-Gaia Light Curve package, we stack the residuals along curved trial paths and link detections across sectors. We identify eleven new TNOs, each detected blindly in two to five TESS sectors and independently in archival ground-based images, with arcs of 2-20 years. They have V = 20.8-22.1, heliocentric distances of 25-57 au, inclinations of 16-27 deg, and diameters of about 120-910 km for an assumed albedo of 0.08. They lie 9-26 deg from the ecliptic, and the largest is 5 deg from the Galactic plane. Eight additional objects linked across two or three TESS sectors lack secure independent recovery in the archives examined and remain candidates. The search recovers 314 known TNOs and Centaurs, with an empirical recovery fraction of 50% at V = 21.6 before quality cuts. Nine were discovered after TESS imaged them, including 2026 ED138 6.8 years before its discovery by Rubin. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of TESS for finding bright outer Solar System objects and extending their observational arcs.

papers.title: Quantum Efficiency Measurements of a Low-Cost, Commercial CMOS Sensor in the Soft X-ray Bandpass
papers.micro: We find a quantum efficiency of roughly 10 – 40% over this band…
papers.abstract: Complementary metal-oxide semiconductor (CMOS) image sensors offer distinct advantages as imaging detectors for space-based X-ray observatories, being low-power, radiation-resistant, and operable at room temperature. Previous characterizations of the low-cost, commercially-available IMX290LLR-C back-illuminated CMOS sensor from Sony Semiconductor Solutions have found Fano-limited X-ray spectral resolutions while operated at room temperature and a radiation tolerance compatible with use in low Earth orbit. Here, we report the quantum efficiency of the IMX290LLR-C as measured across the soft X-ray band (200 - 1000 eV) using Beamline 6.3.2 of the Advanced Light Source at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory. We find a quantum efficiency of roughly 10 – 40% over this band, and fit these measurements to a quantum efficiency model constrained by these measurements and microscopy of the sensor layers. These measurements and the derived model informs this sensor's application within low-cost X-ray observatories, as well as motivates the development of commercial X-ray CMOS sensors without microlenses and deeper Si depletion layers.

papers.title: TOI-1699A: a sub-Neptune and a super-Jovian in an S-type planetary system
papers.micro: TOI-1699A joins the still limited sample of S-type multiplanet systems…
papers.abstract: We present the detection and characterization of the TOI-1699A (TYC 3415-00428-1) S-type planetary system, hosted by the G5 V primary of a wide binary with an M3 V stellar companion at a projected separation of ∼348 au. The inner planet, TOI-1699A b, was initially detected by TESS and confirmed with targeted CHEOPS photometry, ground-based photometry, and HARPS-N follow-up. With an orbital period of ∼4.55 d, radius of 3.096^+0.057_−0.056 R⊕, mass of 13.9^+1.9_−1.8 M⊕, and bulk density of 2.58^+0.40_−0.39 g cm⁻³, TOI-1699A b lies firmly in the sub-Neptune regime and requires a substantial volatile envelope. The HARPS-N data additionally reveal a massive outer companion, TOI-1699A c, with an orbital period of 108.75 ± 0.10 days, a low but significant eccentricity of 0.0737 ± 0.0034, and a minimum mass of 5.54 ± 0.21 MJup. Assuming coplanarity with the inner planet, TOI-1699A c is not expected to transit, and our dynamical stability analysis disfavors a stellar-mass nature and limits its true mass to Mc ≲ 18 MJup. Our combined data-driven and dynamical detection-limit analysis excludes additional planets between 54 and 235 days, and planets more massive than 27 M⊕ at shorter periods. TOI-1699A joins the still limited sample of S-type multiplanet systems, while upcoming Gaia DR4 astrometry together with radial velocity monitoring can constrain the true mass and inclination of the outer planet.

papers.title: Precise Deep-Learning Reconstruction of Galaxy Cluster Mass Maps and Substructures from Optical Observations
papers.micro: The model is inherently flexible and can incorporate multi-wavelength observations, including X-ray and Sunyaev–Zel'dovich data, to further improve total mass predictions.
papers.abstract: Accurately mapping the total mass distribution within galaxy clusters, including dark matter, is fundamental to understanding structure formation and constraining cosmological parameters. Conventional mass-mapping techniques rely predominantly on gravitational lensing and often produce smooth mass distributions based on analytical profiles, potentially missing important internal substructures. We introduce a complementary, simulation-based inference approach to reconstruct detailed galaxy cluster mass maps and resolve their internal substructures directly from optical imaging. We trained deep learning models on realistic hydrodynamical simulations of galaxy clusters to infer their mass distributions from optical observations. We subsequently applied this framework to observations of real galaxy clusters obtained with the Hubble Space Telescope (HST) as part of the Cluster Lensing And Supernova survey with Hubble (CLASH) programme. The reconstructed mass maps successfully reproduce the overall shapes and radial mass profiles of the CLASH clusters, showing strong agreement with independent gravitational lensing measurements. Furthermore, the subhalo mass functions derived from the reconstructed maps exhibit power-law behaviour broadly consistent with predictions from numerical simulations. Our results demonstrate that combining optical imaging with deep learning provides a scalable and physically meaningful approach to mapping galaxy cluster mass distributions. This framework opens a new avenue for exploiting upcoming wide-field imaging surveys to systematically investigate dark matter substructures across large cluster samples, complementing traditional gravitational lensing techniques. Moreover, the model is inherently flexible and can incorporate multi-wavelength observations, including X-ray and Sunyaev–Zel'dovich data, to further improve total mass predictions.

papers.title: Probing baryonic feedback using fast radio bursts and galaxy surveys
papers.micro: Using HEFT with the Padé model of baryonic feedback, we forecast that next-generation FRB surveys (combined with galaxy samples) will be able to constrain feedback at a level…
papers.abstract: The dispersion measure (DM) of fast radio bursts (FRB) provides a noisy measure of the free-electron column density to the burst. With next-generation FRB surveys the number of bursts will drastically increase and measurements of the baryon distribution will be possible on the Mpc scales most relevant to Stage IV weak lensing surveys. Comparing the DM auto-spectrum, DM-shear cross-spectrum and the kinetic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect, we argue that the cross-correlation of FRB catalogs with galaxy surveys offers many advantages. Hybrid Effective Field Theory (HEFT), often used in large-scale structure cosmology, is capable of modeling the clustering of electrons jointly with galaxies and matter to small scales. Using HEFT with the Padé model of baryonic feedback, we forecast that next-generation FRB surveys (combined with galaxy samples) will be able to constrain feedback at a level informative for Stage IV weak lensing surveys. In particular we should not be limited by modeling the manner in which galaxies trace the matter field. Rather constraints of the higher-order electron biases and the electron-galaxy cross-stochasticity provide the dominant limitation, and are an obvious target for improvement in order to reach percent-level constraints. The same measurements also provide a valuable means of constraining feedback in hydrodynamic simulations of galaxy formation in a way that is not tied to the modeling of particular galaxy samples.

papers.title: Parity conservation of the isotropic galaxy 4PCF in redshift space
papers.micro: Expanding the 4PCF in spherical harmonics, we show that angular momentum selection rules…
papers.abstract: Recent observational investigation of cosmological Parity Violation (PV) through the galaxy Four-point Correlation Function (4PCF) has motivated a careful theoretical examination of potential systematic contributions. In this work, we demonstrate that parity-odd contributions to the isotropic 4PCF estimator induced by Redshift Space Distortion (RSD), up to the leading order H/k of general relativistic corrections, vanish upon averaging over all the Line-of-Sight (LOS). We analyse the perturbative relativistic galaxy number density, combining the biased tracer expansion and the dark matter gravitational dynamics within the framework of Standard Eulerian Perturbation Theory (EPT) to third order in the density perturbation. Building on prior studies of the parity-odd mode of the trispectrum (the Fourier-space counterpart of the 4PCF), we extend existing results in three directions: incorporating the wide-angle effect by adopting a local LOS definition for each galaxy in the 4PCF, accounting for tidal bias in the galaxy population, and generalising the assessment to an arbitrary cosmological background. Expanding the 4PCF in spherical harmonics, we show that angular momentum selection rules, encoded in the Wigner 3-j symbols, enforce that only parity-even contributions survive the integration over all LOS orientations, both in the plane-parallel approximation and in the full wide-angle case. This result is crucial for large-scale statistical analyses using isotropic estimators. It supports interpreting possible PV detections as a signal not due to a systematic RSD artefact. We conclude with a discussion of the caveats of our results and identify potential sources of PV.

papers.title: Does Dark Energy Evolve and Cluster?
papers.micro: Present data cannot yet determine whether the suggestive low-redshift features in the two sectors share a common physical origin, a question that ongoing Stage-IV surveys will be able to address
papers.abstract: Recent cosmological observations have renewed interest in dynamical dark energy, and naturally raise the question of whether departures from the standard expansion history are accompanied by modifications of gravitational dynamics. We address this question through a joint, non-parametric reconstruction of the effective dark-energy contribution to the expansion and the gravitational responses governing clustering and lensing, complemented by a combined covariance-mode analysis, without imposing model-specific relations between the sectors. Combining CMB, DESI DR2 BAO, and Pantheon+ supernova observations, and subsequently adding large scale structure observations including DES Year 3 6×2pt data and other surveys, we recover a broad maximum in the effective dark-energy density near z≃0.6–0.7. The gravitational responses exhibit suggestive low-redshift enhancements over their GR values, approximately coincident with the background feature. Adding large scale structure information preserves the background feature but favours a mildly reduced lensing response. The combined covariance-mode analysis identifies the combinations of background and gravitational responses most tightly constrained by current observations and quantifies their departures from ΛCDM. The leading modes are decisively background dominated, while the gravitational sector remains less precisely constrained. Thus, present data cannot yet determine whether the suggestive low-redshift features in the two sectors share a common physical origin, a question that ongoing Stage-IV surveys will be able to address

papers.title: Reconstruction of Dynamical Dark Energy and Gravity from latest cosmological data
papers.micro: Current departures from ΛCDM are most significant in the expansion history, while leaving open the possibility of correlated modifications to gravitational dynamics that future Stage IV surveys can test.
papers.abstract: Recent cosmological observations have renewed interest in non-standard late-time evolution. We investigate whether departures from the standard expansion history are accompanied by modifications of gravitational dynamics through a joint, non-parametric reconstruction of the effective dark energy density, ΩX(a), and the gravitational response functions μ(a) and Σ(a). Combining CMB, DESI DR2 BAO, Pantheon+, and large scale structure observations, including DES Year 3 6×2pt data, we perform reconstructions with and without a theory motivated correlation prior derived from stable Horndeski models. We find a persistent maximum in ΩX at z≃0.5–0.7, corresponding to a crossing of the effective phantom divide. This feature is already present in the CMB+BAO combination and remains robust when modifications to clustering and lensing are allowed. The reconstructed gravitational response exhibits suggestive enhancements in μ and Σ over approximately the same redshift range, although these departures are less significant. Including LSS information instead favours a reduced lensing response, Σ<1, while leaving the background feature largely unchanged. An interpretation within Generalized Brans-Dicke theories illustrates how modifications to the effective gravitational coupling and a scalar-mediated fifth force may contribute to these trends. Our results indicate that current departures from ΛCDM are most significant in the expansion history, while leaving open the possibility of correlated modifications to gravitational dynamics that future Stage IV surveys can test.

papers.title: Depletion of Dark Matter Spikes by Massive Black Hole Mergers
papers.micro: Accretion-induced adiabatic MBH growth is unable to cause appreciable spike re-growth between such mergers in Horizon-AGN.
papers.abstract: Dark matter over-densities around massive black holes, known as dark matter spikes, can dephase gravitational waves emitted by intermediate- and extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (IMRIs/EMRIs), offering a promising way to indirectly detect dark matter. This detection channel, however, requires the spike to survive over cosmological time-scales. We investigate the impact that a host black hole's merger history has on its dark-matter spike. We focus on how the inspiral of a massive-black-hole (MBH) binary modifies and disrupts these spikes within the central ∼ 100 Schwarzschild radii of the black hole. We find that a single merger with mass ratio q = 0.03 is capable of reducing a spike's density by around 3 (5) orders of magnitude at 100 (5) Schwarzschild radii across all polar angles relative to the binary's plane, independent of the primary MBH's mass, with larger mass ratios inducing even stronger depletion. In fact, a single past merger with mass ratio as small as q = 0.005 reduces central densities by 2–3 orders of magnitude, making gravitational-wave dephasing difficult to detect. We relate these results to the MBH merger history by analysing cosmological simulation data from Horizon-AGN. We find that mergers become increasingly common as the MBH mass increases, with mergers of mass ratio q > 0.03 having occurred in 50% of MBHs of mass 3×10⁷M☉ and 95% of mass 10⁸M☉ at z=0. These fractions are reached at even lighter masses (2×10⁷M☉ and 5×10⁷M☉, respectively) at z=3. We find that accretion-induced adiabatic MBH growth is unable to cause appreciable spike re-growth between such mergers in Horizon-AGN. Thus, in combination with previous studies of EMRI-induced depletion, this work constrains the mass range over which massive black holes can host detectable DM spikes to 10⁶M☉–5 × 10⁷M☉ for z ≤ 3.

papers.abstract: A full-tensor superconducting gravity gradiometer whose four test masses carry two compositions in a 2+2 pattern acquires a composition-dependent channel for dilaton-coupled ultralight dark matter. The reconstructed response is the rank-one tensor K=gvφ(t)otimesqv, with the axis of qv fixed in advance by the material assignment, and obeys the parameter-free null condition K(I−Pq)=0, which no gravity gradient or platform rotation alone can satisfy; it vanishes for a single composition. papers.title: Composition-dependent ultralight dark matter detection with a tetrahedral superconducting gravity gradiometer
papers.micro: Giving the four test masses two compositions in a 2+2 arrangement adds a composition-dependent ultralight dark matter (ULDM) channel to that same tensor readout…
papers.abstract: Tetrahedral superconducting gravity gradiometers designed as full-tensor gravitational-wave detectors, such as the ground-based mSOGRO design and the proposed lunar LANGO observatory, reconstruct the acceleration-gradient tensor from four test masses. We show that giving the four test masses two compositions in a 2+2 arrangement adds a composition-dependent ultralight dark matter (ULDM) channel to that same tensor readout, with no separate dark-matter sensor and no dark-matter-specific readout. A coherently oscillating scalar accelerates each mass in proportion to its dilaton charge, and the tensor reconstruction leaves the charges only in a mean, rejected with the common mode, and a single vector qv proportional to the charge contrast ΔabaralphaAB between the two materials. The response is the rank-one tensor K_ULDM(t)=gvφ(t)otimesqv, whose amplitude is set by the halo, independent of mφ. The axis of qv is fixed in advance by the material assignment, so the response obeys the null condition K_ULDM(I−Pq)=0 at every instant, for any gvφ including a virialized field with a stochastic gradient—an exact tensor discriminator against gravitational-wave signals; for a single composition qv=0. With the gravitational-wave noise model, the coupling sensitivity for copper and lead test masses reaches dm−dg≃3.4×10⁻⁸ for the baseline instrument and 4.9×10⁻¹⁰ with upgraded accelerometers. The rank-one factorization and the null condition are summarized in a companion Letter; the present paper gives the derivations and the detector-level analysis.

papers.title: Microscopic Realizability of Non-unique Bubble Hydrodynamics
papers.micro: We identify microscopic settings that realize these sound-speed hierarchies.
papers.abstract: First-order phase transitions drive fluid motion that induces energy transport and gravitational-wave production. The flows are usually classified in terms of the wall velocity and the transition strength. We show that this description fails when the two phases have unequal sound speeds c±. New mixed-hybrid profiles may appear, and for a strong hierarchy, c₊≫ c₋, where the phase behind the wall is much softer, heating or cooling ahead of the wall allow for the coexistence of distinct stationary flows at the same wall velocity and transition strength. This ambiguity is removed once thermodynamic normalization and entropy production are specified. We identify microscopic settings that realize these sound-speed hierarchies. In thermal plasmas it requires exponentially large mass-to-temperature ratios, whereas at finite density a conserved charge removes this obstruction, making dense matter its natural arena.

papers.title: Hydr'oDex: gotta match 'em all!
papers.micro: We present a comprehensive hydrodynamic classification of stationary fluid profiles in first-order phase transitions within the constant-sound-speed model…
papers.abstract: We present a comprehensive hydrodynamic classification of stationary fluid profiles in first-order phase transitions within the constant-sound-speed model, a physically motivated extension of the standard bag model that allows the sound speeds in front of and behind the wall, c₊ and c₋, to differ. Solving the matching conditions at the bubble wall and evolving the profile in the surrounding plasma, we systematically identify and classify all the possible stationary solutions. The classification recovers all previously known direct and inverse detonation, deflagration, and hybrid solutions, while revealing a new class of stationary configurations, termed mixed hybrids, featuring rarefaction waves on both sides of the wall and oppositely directed fluid flows. For a sufficiently pronounced hierarchy c₊ > c₋, the classification in terms of the wall velocity ξw and the asymptotic strength parameter αN further exhibits degenerate regions in parameter space, where multiple distinct stationary profiles correspond to the same physical inputs (ξw,αN). This non-uniqueness arises as the parametrization discards thermodynamic information and is resolved once the underlying microphysics is specified. We also compute the kinetic-energy budget and the associated acoustic gravitational-wave spectra within the sound-shell model, finding that mixed-hybrid solutions, despite their oppositely directed flows, introduce no additional spectral feature, and their spectra can be closely mimicked by ordinary direct or inverse hybrids with very different fluid profiles. Finally, we release HydróDex, a public code that implements the complete hydrodynamic classification, fluid-profile construction, kinetic-energy budget, and gravitational-wave calculation.

papers.title: Many-body Response to Spin-Independent and Spin-Dependent Dark Matter Scattering in a Superfluid Helium-3 Target
papers.micro: We present a first-principles calculation of the DM scattering rate in this inherently quantum many-body medium for both spin-independent and spin-dependent interactions.
papers.abstract: The QUEST-DMC experiment employs an ultra-low-temperature superfluid ³He target in an effort to detect sub-GeV dark matter (DM). The low-momentum scattering of such light DM is sensitive to the many-body structure of superfluid ³He, making it necessary to account for the collective behaviour of the medium. We present a first-principles calculation of the DM scattering rate in this inherently quantum many-body medium for both spin-independent and spin-dependent interactions. The leading consequence of this many-body behaviour is a kinematic enhancement of the scattering rate arising from the Fermi-Dirac statistics of the ultra-low-temperature target. Accounting for this extends the projected reach to lower DM masses for both spin-independent and spin-dependent interactions under the benchmark detector assumptions considered here. The resulting sensitivity improvement becomes increasingly pronounced as the detector threshold drops into the sub-eV regime. It is negligible at the conventional readout threshold of approximately 31 eV, but becomes significant at the 0.51 eV benchmark threshold for SQUID-based readout. Specifically, at this threshold, incorporating the many-body response extends the higher-energy recoil tail and improves the projected low-mass reach by approximately 2.5% relative to the single-atom approximation. This improvement becomes more pronounced at lower thresholds. Reaching a threshold of 5 meV could further extend the sensitivity of QUEST-DMC into the realm of sub-MeV DM.

papers.title: Resonant Trapping of Neutrinophilic Dark Matter in Supernovae
papers.micro: In particular, we show that for mediator masses comparable to the supernova core temperature…
papers.abstract: Supernova cooling provides some of the strongest constraints on light particles beyond the Standard Model, including sub-GeV dark matter (DM). While sufficiently large couplings to the Standard Model sector can trap these particles inside the supernova or cause them to decay before escaping, there typically exists an intermediate range of couplings in which their efficient production and subsequent escape lead to excessive energy loss, resulting in stringent constraints on new light particles. In this work, we demonstrate for the first time that, for certain types of DM-neutrino interactions, resonantly enhanced s-channel scattering with neutrinos can efficiently trap DM inside the supernova and can fundamentally alter the conventional supernova cooling constraints. In particular, we show that for mediator masses comparable to the supernova core temperature, this resonant scattering can prevent a substantial fraction of the produced DM from freely escaping, thereby significantly weakening, or even evading, the usual supernova cooling constraints on such models.

papers.title: ⁸B Solar Neutrino Measurements of Solar Core Size and Temperature from 5805 Days of Super-Kamiokande
papers.micro: In the high metallicity scenario assuming nominal solar core density and solar core size…
papers.abstract: The detection of solar neutrino provides direct evidence for on-going fusion in the core of the Sun and serve as a probe for that solar core. Production rate of ⁸B is sensitive to the solar core temperature. Adiabatic flavor conversion of ⁸B solar neutrinos depends on the local solar electron density. Combined with the roughly exponential decrease in solar electron density with increasing distance from the center of the solar sphere, the solar core size, density, and temperature are inferred. This article presents an outer bound on solar core size and measurements of the density and temperature in the solar core based on Super-Kamiokande phase I-IV solar neutrino data. An outer bound is set for the solar core at 90% confidence level as 0.499R☉ for the high metallicity B16+GS98 Standard Solar Model and 0.381R☉ for K2-A09-MZvar-12 which includes protosolar accretion. A combined fit with the SNO polynomial coefficients improves the limit to 0.268R☉ for B16+GS98 and 0.215R☉ for K2-A09-MZvar-12. Results for other metallicity cases are also reported. In the high metallicity scenario assuming nominal solar core density and solar core size, temperature at the solar center is reported at TC=(15.599±0.0016)×10⁶ K and Tnpz=(15.492±0.0017)×10⁶ K at the peak radius of the ⁸B production profile.

papers.title: Improved Bounds on the Dark Matter-Neutrino Cross Section using LSBGs
papers.micro: Applying our new method to LSBGs, we derive an upper limit of σνχ< 8.5 × 10⁻²⁵ cm² for a dark matter mass of mχ=1 GeV at a typical…
papers.abstract: We derive new constraints on the interaction cross section between dark matter and neutrinos (σνχ) that improve upon existing limits. We adopt a mechanism where neutrinos emitted from core-collapse supernovae transfer their energy to the dark matter halo via elastic scattering, transitioning a centrally cusped profile to a flat-cored profile. We apply this mechanism to Low Surface Brightness Galaxies (LSBGs), which are characterized by their relatively large sizes, low stellar densities, and measurements of dark matter cores. We improve upon previous methods so that each dark matter particle is counted at most once, which weakens existing limits, e.g., from the Fornax dSph by a factor of ∼ 50. Applying our new method to LSBGs, we derive an upper limit of σνχ< 8.5 × 10⁻²⁵  cm² for a dark matter mass of mχ=1  GeV at a typical supernova neutrino energy of Eν=15  MeV. This constraint is approximately three orders of magnitude stronger than the Fornax limit derived with the same method and slightly stronger than the bound from the dark matter diffused supernova neutrino background (DMDSNB).
